g12-chemistry-uc5-t1.overview: Environmental chemistry studies the chemicals around us — where they come from, what they become, and what they do — across the atmosphere, hydrosphere, geosphere and biosphere. This opening topic maps the compartments, the natural cycles that move matter between them, and the chemistry tools (sampling, analysis, risk) used to keep the whole system honest.
objectives: Name the environmental compartments and how chemicals move between them
Describe the water, carbon and nitrogen cycles in chemical terms
Define pollutant, contaminant, source and receptor
Explain sampling, detection limits and monitoring logic
Relate environmental chemistry to Ethiopian contexts (rivers, lakes, soils)
g12-chemistry-uc5-t1.simple: Everything goes somewhere. There is no 'away'. A molecule spilled in Accia Kara river is chemistry for the lake, the floodplain soil, the crops and the cattle that drink. Environmental chemistry follows the atoms: air (atmosphere), water (hydrosphere), ground (geosphere) and life (biosphere) exchange matter in cycles — water evaporates and rains, carbon respires and fixes, nitrogen fizzes and nitrates — and we measure the flow with sampling, instruments and limits.
g12-chemistry-uc5-t1.detailed:
Compartments and transfer. The environment is four linked reactors. Between them chemicals partition: volatile compounds evaporate from water to air (think petrol smell), heavy metals bind to sediment particles and sink, pesticides adsorb to soil organic matter or leach to groundwater. Fugacity — the tendency to escape a phase — predicts the direction; the octanol-water partition coefficient (K_ow) predicts whether a compound concentrates in fat (persistent organic pollutants are all high-K_ow).

The big cycles, chemically. WATER: evaporation (pure H₂O up) − condensation/precipitation − runoff − infiltration; it moves everything else. CARBON: photosynthesis (6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂) vs respiration/combustion (reverse); oceans dissolve CO₂ as carbonic acid/bicarbonate; fossil carbon is a slow-cycle leak that humans reopened. NITROGEN: N₂ → (lightning, rhizobia, Haber) fixed NH₃/NO₃⁻ → plants → animals → denitrification back to N₂; human fertilizer now fixes more nitrogen than all natural processes combined.

Vocabulary of harm. Contaminant: any chemical where/when it shouldn't be. Pollutant: at levels causing harm. Point source (a tannery pipe) vs non-point (farm runoff everywhere). Receptor: the human, fish or crop that meets it. Dose makes the poison: concentration × exposure time; hence safe limits (WHO drinking-water guideline values, Ethiopian standards) and terms like LC₅₀, threshold, bioaccumulation (per organism) vs biomagnification (up the food chain — mercury in fish).

Measurement discipline. Sample representatively (time and place bias ruin data), preserve it (cool, dark, acidified for metals), analyse with graded sensitivity: gravimetry/volumetry for gross stuff (hardness by EDTA titration), colorimetry/spectrophotometry for nutrients (ppm nitrate, phosphate), AAS/ICP for trace metals (ppb lead), GC-MS for organics. Quality control: blanks, duplicates, calibration. What isn't measured can't be managed.

Ethiopian frame. Lake Zara and the Rift lakes (salinity/fluoride), the Akaki river receiving Addis industry and sewage, Gulf of Tadjourah-level sediment in Lake Tana's inflows from coffee-plot erosion, Rift Valley geothermal emissions — the curriculum's local cases all live in these compartments.

workedExamples.problem: Drinking water shows 0.08 mg/L lead. That is how many ppb?
workedExamples.calculation: 1 ppb = 1 µg/L in water ⇒ 0.08 mg/L = 80 µg/L.
workedExamples.answer: 80 ppb — WHO guideline is 10: eight times over, unsafe.

workedExamples.problem: A lake receives 2.5 kg/day phosphate from a town. Annual load?
workedExamples.answer: ≈ 910 kg P/yr — enough to eutrophify a small lake (limits are in parts per billion).

workedExamples.problem: DDT has high K_ow. Where does it end up after spraying?
workedExamples.calculation: High fat affinity: adsorbs to soil organic matter, dissolves in lipids, resists water washing.
workedExamples.answer: Body fat and food chains — the bioaccumulation warning.

workedExamples.problem: A sample splits 1:100 and still shows pollution. Which source type?
workedExamples.calculation: Dilution resistance means continuous diffuse input, not one pipe slug.
workedExamples.answer: Likely non-point (runoff) — one-time spills wash out.

commonMistakes: Treating compartments as isolated (chemicals ALWAYS migrate)
Confusing bioaccumulation (within an organism) with biomagnification (across trophic levels)
Saying 'chemical-free' (everything is chemicals; the issue is dose and identity)
Sampling only from clean-looking sites and declaring safety
Reading ppm as percent anywhere near drinking-water standards
applications: Akaki/Zara river monitoring by Addis universities and EPA-ET
Drinking-water fluoride mapping in Rift Valley boreholes
Environmental Impact Assessments for dams, industry and floriculture
g12-chemistry-uc5-t1.summary: Four compartments, three cycles, one rule: matter moves and dose decides. Measure properly, then manage.

questions.q: Which is a point source of pollution?
questions.explanation: One identifiable location vs diffuse.

questions.q: 1 ppm in dilute water equals:
questions.explanation: 1 mg per litre ≈ one part per million.

questions.q: The phosphorus cycle's bottleneck is that P mainly cycles through:
options: rocks, soil and water (no gas phase)
questions.explanation: Unlike C and N, phosphorus has no significant atmospheric pool.

questions.q: High K_ow indicates a compound likely to:
questions.explanation: Octanol = fat proxy: it prefers lipids.

questions.q: Which fixes nitrogen industrially?
questions.explanation: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃: fertilizer's origin.

questions.q: Mercury in a large predatory fish exceeding pond-water levels thousand-fold is:
questions.explanation: Each trophic step concentrates the indigestible fraction.

questions.q: Best practice for a trace-metal water sample:
questions.explanation: Acid keeps metals dissolved; containers must not leach blank values.

questions.q: Human reactive-nitrogen creation now roughly:
questions.explanation: Haber fertilizer doubled the global N cycle — a textbook anthropocene shift.

g12-chemistry-uc5-t2.overview: Pollution by medium: air (smog, SO₂, NOx, particulates, CO₂), water (pathogens, nutrients, organics, metals), soil and land (pesticides, salinization, mine tailings) — with the chemistry behind each, how it is measured (AQI, BOD, COD), and the control technologies that turn waste streams back into manageable chemistry.
objectives: Write the key air-pollution reactions (SO₂, NOx, photochemical smog, CO)
Explain acid rain formation and effects
Define and apply BOD/COD for water organic load
Describe eutrophication chemistry step by step
Summarise pollution-control: scrubbers, catalysts, treatment stages
g12-chemistry-uc5-t2.simple: Four battlegrounds. Air: burning fuel makes CO₂ + heat, but imperfectly also CO, soot, SO₂ (from sulfur in oil/coal) and NOx (nitrogen + oxygen, hot-engine special) — which combine with sunlight into smog. Water: organic waste feeds bacteria that eat dissolved oxygen (measured as BOD); fish suffocate. Nutrients (n/p) feed algae that do the same at night. Soil: pesticides and heavy metals persist, adsorb, and creep up food chains. Each medium has a control playbook.
g12-chemistry-uc5-t2.detailed:
Air chemistry. S + O₂ → SO₂; SO₂ further oxidises (OH• in cloudwater or catalysed on particles) to H₂SO₄ aerosol. N₂ + O₂ → 2NO (only at flame/high-T: cars, power plants), NO + ½O₂ → NO₂, brown and itchy. NO₂ + hν → NO + O•; O• + O₂ → O₃: ground-level ozone — smog's oxidising main actor (good upstairs in the stratosphere, bad downstairs). Hydrocarbons + NOx + sunlight = PAN and photochemical smog (LA 1940s, Addis and industrial towns now on a smaller scale). CO from oxygen-starved combustion binds haemoglobin 200× tighter than O₂. Particulates (PM₂.₅) carry everything and reach deep lung.

Acid rain. SO₂ + OH•/O₃ → H₂SO₄; 2NO₂ + •OH → HNO₃ in cloud droplets: rain pH 4.2–4.5 vs natural 5.6 (already acidic from dissolved CO₂: carbonic acid). Damage: carbonate buildings and frescoes (CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ crust + flaking), lake acidification (Al³⁺ leached from soil — whose hydrolysis is what truly kills fish), soil nutrient leaching. Controls: coal desulfurization, lime scrubbers, catalytic converters upstream.

Water: organic load. Bacteria oxidise waste: (CH₂O)ₙ + nO₂ → nCO₂ + nH₂O. How much O₂ the bugs will consume = Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD₅, 5 days, 20 °C, mg/L); the chemical version (hot dichromate oxidises everything) = COD > BOD. Untreated sewage BOD ~300 mg/L; river self-purification restores downstream IF the load stays under the flow's oxygen budget — otherwise the water goes septic (black, anaerobic, H₂S-smelling).

Eutrophication chain. N/P from fertilizer, sewage, detergents → algal bloom (surface green soup) → algae die and sink → bacteria decompose them using O₂ → hypoxia/azoxia → fish kills, dead zones (Gulf of Mexico classic). Some blooms also release toxins (cyanobacteria in reservoirs). The Ethiopian parallel: nutrient loads in Lake Tana's tributaries from coffee-wash water; Zara near Addis is already past this movie's climax.

Soil and hazardous waste. Pesticides: organochlorines (DDT) persistent + bioaccumulative — banned; organophosphates (malathion) acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, faster to degrade but acutely toxic — handle with respect. Metals: Pb (petrol, paints), Cd (batteries, phosphate fertilizer), Hg (mining — gold extraction still uses it in some Ethiopian artisanal sites) — bind to organic matter, taken up by crops, and never destroyed. Control now: sanitation (sewage works: primary settling → secondary activated-sludge/aerobic ponds (huge BOD cut) → tertiary: nutrient removal, disinfection (chlorine, UV, ozone — each with trade-offs)); air: scrubbers (SO₂ + limestone → CaSO₃), three-way catalytic converters (CO + HC + NOx → CO₂ + H₂O + N₂), electrostatic precipitators (particles); solid waste: landfill design vs recycling chemistry.

keyTerms.def: sunlight-driven NOx + HC soup incl. O₃, PAN
oxygen demand: bio vs chemical oxidation of waste

workedExamples.problem: Sewage BOD 260 mg/L, river background 3 mg/L, mixing dilutes to 18 mg/L. Why worry?
workedExamples.calculation: 18 > natural clean levels (≤5); bacteria will strip that oxygen downstream.
workedExamples.answer: Fish-stress zone: load exceeds self-purification; needs treatment not just dilution.

workedExamples.problem: A car's catalytic converter treats CO: write the oxidation and say why it's exothermic.
workedExamples.answer: Converts lethal CO to CO₂; the canister runs hot.

workedExamples.problem: Liming a lake: Ca(OH)₂ neutralises acid: what does it fix chemically?
workedExamples.calculation: Raises pH; Al³⁺ precipitates as Al(OH)₃ so its toxic hydrolysis stops.
workedExamples.answer: Both acidity and the dissolved aluminium that does the real killing.
Solid calcium sulfite/sulfate caught, CO₂ released: 90%+ SO₂ removed.

commonMistakes: Calling ground-level ozone 'the good kind' (stratosphere blocks UV; troposphere scars lungs)
Confusing BOD (oxygen) with COD (dichromate) — COD is always larger
Blaming eutrophication on algae alone: the O₂ crash comes from the DECOMPOSERS
Acid rain starting at pH 7 (natural rain is already 5.6 from CO₂)
Treating dilution as a solution ('the river cleans it') beyond the oxygen budget
applications: Addis sewage: Kality/Kotebi ponds' BOD removal
Flour mill and tannery effluent rules (chrome in Akaki sediment)
Cook-stove and household air pollution (indoor PM₂.₅ from charcoal)
Cement kiln and refinery air-quality permits
g12-chemistry-uc5-t2.summary: S→SO₂→acid; NOx+sun→O₃; waste→BOD→anoxia; P→bloom→dead zone. Every pollutant has a reaction chain — and a control technology.

questions.q: Ground-level ozone forms mainly from:
questions.explanation: Traffic NOx + sunlight is the smog engine.

questions.q: CO's toxicity comes from:
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin starves the blood of oxygen.

questions.q: Natural rain is slightly acidic (pH 5.6) because:
questions.explanation: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃: baseline before any SO₂/NOx.

questions.q: A water sample with high BOD means:
questions.explanation: BOD = how much O₂ microbes will steal: demand, not supply.

questions.q: Fish kills in eutrophied lakes occur mainly because:
options: bacterial decay of dead algae strips O₂
water is too green to see
questions.explanation: The decomposers' oxygen bill arrives after the bloom crashes.

questions.q: Which removes SO₂ from flue gas?
questions.explanation: Basic CaCO₃/Ca(OH)₂ wash traps acidic SO₂ as sulfite.

questions.q: Catalytic converters do NOT reduce:
questions.explanation: The reaction PRODUCES CO₂ while destroying CO.

questions.q: DDT was banned largely because it:
questions.explanation: Persistence + fat-solubility + food-chain amplification.

g12-chemistry-uc5-t3.overview: The greenhouse effect is basic physics: some molecules absorb the Earth's outgoing infrared and reradiate it downward, warming the surface. Natural and life-enabling; human-enhanced and now dangerous. This topic covers the carbon-cycle arithmetic, the evidence, the climate chemistry (feedbacks, oceans, ozone), and the mitigation chemistry — energy, fuels, capture and storage — Ethiopia pursues.
objectives: Explain why CO₂/CH₄/H₂O/N₂O absorb IR (bond vibration logic)
Trace the enhanced greenhouse effect to fossil-carbon release
Read CO₂ trends (~280 → 420+ ppm) and the greenhouse-gas list
Describe key feedbacks and ocean acidification chemistry
Outline mitigation: renewables, efficiency, carbon capture, Ethiopia's CRGE
g12-chemistry-uc5-t3.simple: Blankets made of molecules. Earth radiates heat as infrared; CO₂'s bonds vibrate in rhythm with those frequencies and reradiate some heat back down — a one-blanket planet would be −18 °C without it, and life exists because of it. Problem: we burn concentrated ancient carbon fast (fossil fuels), thickening the blanket by +50% CO₂ since 1850, +~1.2 °C so far. Methane is fewer molecules but a fiercer blanket; N₂O from fertilizer, too.
g12-chemistry-uc5-t3.detailed:
The mechanism. Greenhouse gases (GHGs) must be vibrationally active in the IR: heteronuclear bonds (C=O, O-H, C-H) change dipole as they stretch/bend and can absorb photons; N₂ and O₂ (homonuclear, no dipole change) are transparent. H₂O (natural, feedback) > CO₂ (long-lived driver) > CH₄ (80× stronger per molecule over 20 yr, ~12 yr lifetime) > N₂O (centuries) > CFCs (potent, ozone-linked). The atmosphere is transparent to incoming visible light but partly opaque to outgoing IR: surface + lower air warm until radiation escapes.

Carbon-cycle bookkeeping. Pre-industrial air: ~590 Gt C (280 ppm). Fossil reservoirs added ~2 500 Gt C since 1850 at ~10 Gt/yr: about half stays air (now ~420+ ppm, +50% and rising ~2.4 ppm/yr), the rest taken by oceans (carbonic/bicarbonate reaction) and land plants (CO₂ fertilisation). Ocean uptake = ~30% of our CO₂ but pays with ACIDIFICATION: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻; surface-ocean pH fell 8.2 → 8.1 (looks small — but it's +30% H⁺), dissolving carbonate shells (CaCO₃ saturation dropping; corals and plankton pay).

Feedbacks. Water-vapour: warmer air holds more H₂O (more blanket) — amplifies. Ice-albedo: melting bright ice exposes dark ocean absorbing more. Permafrost: thaw releases CH₄/CO₂ from stored carbon. Clouds: net uncertain, likely amplifying. These decide sensitivity — the consensus: doubling CO₂ ⇒ ~3 °C ± 1.5 warming, and current pledges point past 2 °C without faster action.

Evidence beyond thermometers. Ice cores (Law Dome: CO₂ and temperature locked in step over 800 000 yr, CO₂ never above 300 ppm until industrial), isotope fingerprint (fossil carbon is ¹³C/¹⁴C-free — the exact signature dropping from air and biosphere: our carbon is diluting theirs), ocean heat content (90% of the excess went to water), shrinking ice sheets and glaciers (the Bale Mountains' past glaciation already gone), accelerating sea-level rise (thermal expansion + melt), and longer fire/hot extremes. No single measurement needs trust: they cross-check.

Mitigation chemistry. Energy: solar/wind/hydro/geothermal emit no process carbon; GERD dams (Ethiopia's grid ≈ 90%+ renewable — one of the world's lowest per-capita footprints) and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam put ~5 GW hydro on a grid that mostly burned none before. Fuels: hydrogen (fuel cells: 2H₂+O₂→2H₂O electricity), biofuels from waste, e-fuels (CO₂ + green H₂). Efficiency: insulation, motors (the cheapest carbon). Removal: direct air capture (huge dilution problem — 420 ppm is 0.04%: scrubbing air is energy-hungry), enhanced weathering/afforestation (Ethiopia's Green Legacy: billions of seedlings — carbon sinks with soil/water co-benefits), and adaptation (climate-smart agriculture, early-warning). Ozone layer note: the Montreal Protocol proved global chemistry treaties CAN work — CFCs banned, the ozone hole is healing.

keyTerms.def: IR-absorbing gases return heat to surface
¹⁴C-free CO₂ = fossil carbon in the air
scrub, pipe, store or use the CO₂

formulas.name: Ocean acid
formulas.meaning: the sea drinks CO₂ and sours

formulas.name: Fossil-carbon math
formulas.meaning: each tonne of carbon makes 3.7 t CO₂

workedExamples.problem: Burning 1 tonne of carbon emits how many tonnes CO₂?
workedExamples.answer: ≈ 3.7 t CO₂ — why coal is the dirtiest fuel per joule.

workedExamples.problem: If 10 Gt C/yr emitted and air retains ~4.5, where's the rest?
workedExamples.answer: ~2.5 Gt ocean, ~3 Gt land plants (fertilisation) — until those sinks saturate.

workedExamples.problem: Methane's 20-year GWP ~80 vs CO₂ 1: why target methane cuts first?
workedExamples.calculation: CH₄ lives ~12 yr: cutting it cools fast; CO₂ accumulates for centuries.
workedExamples.answer: Quick wins on the near-term curve while the long game continues.

commonMistakes: Claiming 'CO₂ is only 0.04% so it can't matter' (tiny in %, huge in radiative lines: trace gases drive the blanket)
Confusing the ozone hole with climate change (related CFC chemistry, different problems)
Thinking natural cycles explain the rise (isotopes prove it's fossil carbon)
Reading +0.1 pH as negligible
Believing greenhouse effect = evil (it keeps us alive; the ENHANCED effect is the crisis)
applications: Ethiopia's CRGE and Green Legacy: adaptation + sink building
GERD: replacing imported diesel/kerosene lighting with zero-carbon power
Cook-stove programs: black-carbon and health wins together
Carbon markets and payments for watershed restoration (soil + tree chemistry)
g12-chemistry-uc5-t3.summary: IR-active molecules blanket the planet; +50% CO₂ (fossil, isotope-proofed) ⇒ +1.2 °C, souring seas, feedbacks amplifying. Chemistry also builds the exits: renewables, methane cuts, capture, sinks.

questions.q: Which gas does NOT absorb infrared?
questions.explanation: N₂: homonuclear, no dipole change, invisible to IR.

questions.q: Pre-industrial CO₂ was about:
questions.explanation: 280 ppm; now 420+.

questions.q: Ocean acidification directly reduces:
questions.explanation: H⁺ converts CO₃²⁻ to HCO₃⁻: builders (corals, plankton) short of material.

questions.q: The isotope evidence that extra CO₂ is fossil is its lack of:
questions.explanation: Ancient carbon lost all ¹⁴C; the air's ¹⁴C ratio is falling exactly as CO₂ rises.

questions.q: Melting ice accelerating warming is:
questions.explanation: Dark surfaces replace reflective ones: more absorption, more melt.

questions.q: The largest share of human-caused warming comes from:
questions.explanation: ~2/3+ of the forcing: CO₂ — from sheer mass and lifetime.

questions.q: Cutting methane helps climate quickly because it:
questions.explanation: Short-lived but fierce: cuts cool within years, not centuries.

questions.q: Direct air capture is energy-hungry mainly because:
questions.explanation: Concentrating 420 ppm to pure CO₂ means processing mountainous volumes of air.

g12-chemistry-uc5-t4.overview: Green chemistry redesigns products and processes so pollution is never made — twelve principles (prevent waste, atom economy, safer solvents, catalysis, degrade-in-place design) that flip the old end-of-pipe logic. Applied from pharma to the Ethiopian beverage sector, it is where Unit 3's industrial chemistry meets Unit 5's environmental conscience.
objectives: State the 12 principles and apply the core five
Compute atom economy and relate it to E-factor
Contrast end-of-pipe treatment with design-out prevention
Give examples of green solvent/catalysis/energy choices
Evaluate Ethiopian industry's green-chemistry moves
g12-chemistry-uc5-t4.simple: The best waste is the one never created. Old model: make stuff, then clean the mess (scrubbers, treatment ponds). Green model: design the reaction so the mess can't exist. Metric: atom economy — how many atoms of your reactants end in the product (additions: 100%; substitutions/eliminations: shed salt). Plus: safer solvents (water, supercritical CO₂), catalysts instead of stoichiometric reagents, room-temperature routes, and products that degrade to harmless things afterwards.
g12-chemistry-uc5-t4.detailed:
The 12 principles (Anastas & Warner, 1998). 1 Prevention, 2 Atom economy, 3 Less-hazardous synthesis, 4 Safer design, 5 Safer solvents/auxiliaries, 6 Energy efficiency, 7 Renewable feedstocks, 8 No unnecessary derivatives (skip protecting groups), 9 Catalysis (over stoichiometric), 10 Design for degradation, 11 Real-time pollution analysis, 12 Accident-prevention chemistry (inherently safer). The exam core: 1, 2, 5, 9, 10 — know a one-line example for each.

Counting waste. Atom economy = (M product / ΣM reactants) × 100%. Addition polymerisation: 100%. Ethanoic acid via methanol carbonylation (CH₃OH + CO → CH₃COOH): 100% — vs old acetate-route stoichiometric oxidants. But yield matters too: real waste is the E-factor (kg waste / kg product): pharma E-factor 25-100, bulk chemicals <1, refining ~0.1. Both metrics + the difference between yield and atom economy is the classic trap.

Greener choices in practice. Solvents: replace chlorinated/aromatic with water, ethanol, or supercritical CO₂ (decaf coffee AND dry-cleaning — from an Ethiopian commodity's cousin). Reagents: H₂O2 oxidations give water as by-product (paper bleaching) vs chlorine's organochlorines. Catalysis: enzymes in detergents (cold wash = principle 6 + 9 in your washing powder); zeolite shape-selective catalysts in refining; catalyst recovery in pharma. Feedstocks: castor-oil derivatives (Ethiopia is a world leader: polyamides, lubricants — sebacic acid from renewable seed vs petrochemical); bio-PET bottles.

Industry stories to retell. Ibuprofen: Hoechst route (1960s) atom economy ~40% with 5 steps and lots of salt → BHC green route (1990s): 3 catalytic steps, ~80% atom economy, and HF catalyst recycled — the textbook before/after. Supercritical-CO₂ extraction of hops and flavours replaces hexane. Poly(lactic acid) compostable packaging from maize/ sugarcane vs persistent PET; design for degradation done right (it degrades in industrial compost, not roadside — nuance).

Ethiopian application. Breweries' spent-grain → animal feed/brandy (distiller's grains: zero-waste circularity); wineries' pomace oil; sugar-mill bagasse burning for power (biomass cogeneration: renewable principle 7); tanneries moving chrome(III) liquor recovery-circularity (the green-chemistry fix for the chrome(III)/Cr(VI) oxidation hazard of Unit 3); floriculture IPM (biological pest control, principle 3/4); and clean-cookstove programs cutting indoor PM and CO. Green chemistry as industrial strategy = less imported reagents, less effluent treatment cost, less forex spent.

keyTerms.def: design-out hazard and waste at the molecular level
% of reactant atoms in the product
kg waste per kg product (real-world score)
treat waste after making it: the model green beats
products that finish as harmless small molecules

formulas.name: Atom economy
formulas.meaning: worth vs waste built into the equation

formulas.name: E-factor
formulas.meaning: kg of everything-else per kg of stuff

workedExamples.problem: CH₃CH₂OH + HBr → C₂H₅Br + H₂O: atom economy for bromoethane (M 109 vs 46+81)?
workedExamples.answer: 86% — water is the only 'waste', already decent; elimination/oxidation routes score far worse.

workedExamples.problem: Route makes 1 kg product but 6 kg total reactants/solvents used. E-factor?
workedExamples.answer: 5 kg waste/kg product — versus <0.5 for modern bulk plants: where to target first (solvents).

workedExamples.problem: Hoechst ibuprofen: 6 steps, ~50% AE; BHC: 3 catalytic steps, ~77% AE plus recycling. Green wins on which principles?
workedExamples.calculation: Compare per-step atom counts and yields: fewer steps, less solvent, higher AE.

workedExamples.problem: Enzyme detergent lets washing at 30 °C instead of 90 °C. Which principles?
workedExamples.answer: Consumer-phase green chemistry: the product itself saves energy.

commonMistakes: Computing atom economy from non-balanced equations or including excess reagents
Confusing high YIELD with high atom economy (a 95%-yield, 40%-AE route still dumps 60% of atoms)
Calling any 'natural' product green (nicotine is natural; toxicity is molecular, not botanical)
Designing degradable products that only degrade in unrealistic conditions (oxo-degradable ≠ compostable)
Ticking the 12 principles like a checklist without metrics (AE/E-factor prove it)
applications: Beverage-sector water/energy recovery and spent-grain feeds
Castor-derived nylons and lubricants (Ethiopian export chemistry)
Wet-process photogravure → digital printing: solvent elimination
g12-chemistry-uc5-t4.summary: Prevention beats cleanup: count atoms (AE) and waste (E-factor), catalyse, pick benign solvents/conditions, design the afterlife. Green chemistry = better engineering, cheaper compliance.

questions.q: Green chemistry's first principle is:
questions.explanation: Better never made than cleaned after.

questions.q: Atom economy for addition reactions (A+B→C) is:
questions.explanation: Every reactant atom lands in the product.

questions.q: Which is the best green SOLVENT choice?
questions.explanation: Non-toxic, non-carcinogenic, cheap — principle 5.

questions.q: A process with 90% yield but 30% atom economy:
options: is efficient: still discards 70% of atoms by design
questions.explanation: Yield ≠ AE: the equation itself wastes atoms; fix the route.

questions.q: Using a catalyst rather than stoichiometric reagent serves principle 9 and also cuts:
questions.explanation: Reagents get consumed to waste; catalysts don't (mass-basis win).

questions.q: E-factor of 25 means:
questions.explanation: The waste-per-product ratio — typical of old-school pharma.

questions.q: Which product feature matches 'design for degradation'?
questions.explanation: Engineered to hydrolyse to benign lactic acid in compost conditions.

questions.q: Supercritical CO₂ extraction is 'green' because the solvent:
options: is non-toxic and leaves no residue when depressurised
questions.explanation: It flashes away as gas; no organic-solvent trace in the product.
